style: Athletic, physical and direct. Senegal combine size, power and pace with a solid defensive structure and dangerous transitions. Strong in duels and set pieces, they rely on explosive forwards and a robust spine, blending experience with youthful athleticism.
recent_form: Arrive for their third consecutive World Cup as arguably Africa's best side and the most potent of the African qualifiers. A star-studded, athletic squad balancing veteran leadership with emerging talent, viewed as serious contenders to advance deep.

key_players.name: Sadio Mane
key_players.note: 34-year-old veteran forward at his last World Cup; pace has faded but retains world-class touch, vision and leadership as the creative heartbeat.

key_players.name: Kalidou Koulibaly
key_players.note: Commanding, experienced defender anchoring the back line; physical and aerially dominant.

key_players.name: Pape Matar Sarr
key_players.note: Tottenham midfielder providing energy, ball progression and box-to-box dynamism in the engine room.

key_players.name: Nicolas Jackson
key_players.note: Powerful, mobile striker offering pace in behind and a focal point for the attack.

key_players.name: Ismaila Sarr
key_players.note: Rapid winger who stretches defenses and provides directness and goal threat on the flank.

key_players.name: Iliman Ndiaye
key_players.note: Skilful, two-footed attacker adding creativity and dribbling in the final third.

historical_news: Won the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations (held in 2022), their first-ever AFCON title, beating Egypt on penalties.
Reached the World Cup quarterfinals on debut in 2002, famously beating defending champions France in the opener.
Reached the round of 16 at the 2022 World Cup despite Sadio Mane being ruled out by injury before the tournament.
The celebrated 'golden generation' narrative around Mane, Koulibaly and a deep pool of European-based talent.
Consistently regarded as Africa's flagship side, qualifying for a third straight World Cup in 2026.
Sadio Mane's farewell tournament storyline as the captain plays his final World Cup.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Positive; widely tipped as Africa's strongest squad alongside Morocco, with the talent and athleticism to make a deep run, though questions linger over Mane's age.
